title: bug: the browser's preview Approve button sends the goal's aggregate id where the daemon expects the preview receipt id
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a from an external review (finding 4, sub-claim B), VERIFIED at HEAD fee4e168 (preview-port.ts has no commits since 51c4a004). This is the control-room half only — NO authority change. The other half (paired browser HUMAN excluded from preview.decide / goal.close by OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS) is a deliberate policy pin under operator ruling comment-18dc557c and the epic rail on Gate kinds; under the owner's 2026-09-09 direction ("one approval at plan time, then unattended") the machine closes those gates by default, so widening that fence is NOT filed here — if a human needs to intervene from the browser it is a separate ruling.

MECHANISM: apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/preview-port.ts:51-54 `previewRefOf` builds the payload's previewRef from the affordance's targetAggregateId (the goal), while the daemon's preview.decide edge resolves previewRef as the preview RECEIPT id; the mismatch answers 422 PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY. The walls are STACKED: the operator-principal fence (403) masks this one for a paired browser user, so "fixing permission alone will not fix that button" — measured true. The receipt id is ALREADY in the browser: needs-you-preview.ts:109 populates facts.receiptId from /preview/read; live-needs-you.tsx:187 does not pass it. preview-port.test.ts:19/:60 use a fixture where targetAggregateId and the asserted previewRef are the SAME string, which is why the defect is green today — that identity is the mutation that reddens the port. preview-approve-live.spec.ts:136-141 has a WALL B arm that currently asserts "refuses".

FIX SHAPE: make PreviewPort.submit take the receipt id explicitly (submit(affordance, receiptId, decision, findings)), build the payload with previewRef: receiptId, pass facts.receiptId from live-needs-you.tsx:187; harden preview-port.test.ts so the fixture's targetAggregateId and the asserted previewRef are DISTINCT strings (e.g. `preview:goal-7` vs a 64-hex id); flip the WALL B arm in preview-approve-live.spec.ts:136-141 from "refuses" to "commits" — that spec decides as the configured OPERATOR by design, so it exercises this fix without touching the fence.

No open board row owns this (task-4cbaca29, DONE, disclosed both walls as follow-up; task-6cbcf5ff, DONE, recorded it as "ALREADY KNOWN … COVERED BY A COMMITTED ARM" — the arm covers the refusal, not the fix). A malformed copy of this row (task-a936f924, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.
definitionOfDone: preview-port.test.ts asserts the submitted payload's previewRef equals the RECEIPT id and NOT the affordance's targetAggregateId, with the two fixture strings made distinct — the arm goes RED against today's previewRefOf and the completion record quotes that red.
The live-needs-you composition passes facts.receiptId through to the port: an arm on the Needs-you preview card asserts the id sent is the one /preview/read answered.

preview-approve-live.spec.ts's WALL B arm asserts the operator's Approve COMMITS a preview decision (not "refuses"), while the WALL A arm (paired non-operator HUMAN -> 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED) is unchanged.

No daemon authority or fence file is touched: git diff on apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts and daemon-command-vocabulary.ts is EMPTY at completion, and the human-approver fence tests are green unedited.

pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test EXIT 0 with its count line quoted (the two mirrors under apps/control-room are invisible to the daemon leg), plus the browser e2e lane for the preview spec with its count line.

implementationPlan.description:
MAKE THE FIXTURE ABLE TO FAIL, AND QUOTE THE RED (DoD 1). Ordered first: this is the mutation that exposes the defect, and once the port is fixed the red is unrecoverable without reverting.

preview-port.test.ts:16-20 sets `targetAggregateId: "preview-goal-7"` and :60 asserts `previewRef: "preview-goal-7"`. THE TWO STRINGS ARE IDENTICAL, so the arm cannot tell which value the port read — that identity is the only reason this defect is green. Make them DISTINCT: keep the affordance's target as a preview-aggregate-shaped string and assert a receipt-shaped id, e.g. a 64-hex value, so the two can never be confused by eye either.

RUN IT AND QUOTE THE RED VERBATIM into a row comment — the failing assertion text, not a summary. DoD 1 asks for exactly that, and a paraphrase does not discharge it.

NO PRODUCTION EDIT IN THIS STEP. The point is to prove the arm can fail against today's `previewRefOf` before anything changes.
implementationPlan.note: DoD 1 pre-fix red captured and quoted verbatim in comment-4c5e7bcd. Made the fixture able to fail: targetAggregateId is now "preview:goal-7" (real previewAggregateId shape, preview-receipt-contracts.ts:88) and a distinct RECEIPT_ID 64-hex const (HEX64 shape, same file:75) is what the arms assert. TWO arms red, not one — the REJECT payload carries previewRef too, so it reds on the same defect. No production edit in this step; only preview-port.test.ts is dirty. Disclosed a pre-existing foreign red in environment-variables-screen.test.tsx (file is CLEAN in git status, so it reds at HEAD, unrelated to this row, not repaired).

implementationPlan.description:
TAKE THE RECEIPT ID EXPLICITLY (preview-port.ts).

Give `PreviewPort.submit` the receipt id as its SECOND parameter — `submit(affordance, receiptId, decision, findings?)` — and build the payload with `previewRef: receiptId`. Delete `previewRefOf`: once the id arrives from the caller there is nothing left to derive.

FOLLOW THE NEIGHBOURS, do not invent a shape. `goal-close-port.submit(OFFER, "goal-1")` and `escalation-port.submit(affordance, nodeKey, decision)` already take an explicit id in that position, so this makes the preview port stop being the odd one out.

REWRITE THE COMMENT AT :49-50, which is the other half of the defect. It currently states the false premise as fact: "The daemon names the preview aggregate as the offer's target, so the decision refers to the preview it was offered for rather than to a ref the browser composed." The daemon resolves `previewRef` as the preview RECEIPT id, and the affordance's target is the goal. Say what is true and say what the failure was — a mismatch answers 422 PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY — so the next reader cannot restore the bug on the strength of a comment.

LEAVE THE REJECT PATH ALONE. The `findings.length === 0` guard returning PREVIEW_FINDINGS_REQUIRED is not this row's subject, and the payload's exact arity on APPROVE stays exactly as the test's `toEqual` pins it.
implementationPlan.note:
PreviewPort.submit now takes the receipt id SECOND — submit(affordance, receiptId, decision, findings?) — matching goal-close-port.submit(affordance, goalId) and escalation-port.submit(affordance, nodeKey, decision). previewRefOf is DELETED; the payload builds previewRef from the parameter. The false comment at :49-50 is replaced with what is true: nothing on the affordance carries the receipt id so it cannot be derived here at all, and the old derivation answered 422 PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY. REJECT path untouched: the findings.length === 0 guard and both payload arities are unchanged and still pinned by toEqual.

A SECOND CALLER EXISTS that step-2's affectedFiles did not name, and a positional insertion breaks it silently — exactly the adversarial question step-5 asks. preview-rejection-invariants.test.tsx:131 called submit(FACTS.affordance, "REJECT", [...]), which would have put "REJECT" in receiptId and the findings array in decision. Fixed to pass FACTS.receiptId, and its assertion now reads previewRef: FACTS.receiptId instead of the hardcoded "preview:goal-1" — so that arm stops being blind to this same defect. live-needs-you.tsx:187 is the third caller and is step-3's subject; typecheck is expected red on it until then.

Both files green: npx vitest run preview-port.test.ts preview-rejection-invariants.test.tsx = Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 11 passed (11).

implementationPlan.description:
PASS THE ID THE BROWSER ALREADY HAS (live-needs-you.tsx) (DoD 2).

live-needs-you.tsx:187 calls `preview.submit(facts.affordance, decision, findings)` while `facts.receiptId` sits right there, populated by needs-you-preview.ts from `/preview/read`. Pass it. That single omission is the entire browser half of the defect.

ADD THE ARM in live-needs-you.test.tsx: the id sent to the port is the one `/preview/read` answered. Assert the VALUE, not that submit was called — a spy that only records a call cannot tell a receipt id from a goal id, which is the same blindness the port fixture had.

Do not change what the card renders or how a decision result is stored. The `setResults` bookkeeping around the call, and the `DECISION_DISPATCH_FAILED` rejection path, are untouched by this row.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 2 delivered. live-needs-you.tsx:191 now passes facts.receiptId — the value needs-you-preview.ts:109 takes from /preview/read — as the port's second argument, with a comment naming the 422 PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY failure so the omission is not restored by a later reader. setResults bookkeeping and the DECISION_DISPATCH_FAILED path are untouched; the card renders identically.

NEW ARM in live-needs-you.test.tsx: "sends the RECEIPT id /preview/read answered, never the offer's aggregate id". It renders a real PREVIEW item (preview.decide offer at preview:goal-plan, readPreview answering STARTED with a 64-hex receiptId), clicks cr.needsyou.preview.approve, and asserts the VALUE: toHaveBeenCalledWith(offer, RECEIPT_ID, "APPROVE", []) plus not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(offer, "preview:goal-plan", ...). A call-count spy would not have discriminated.

NON-VACUITY MEASURED, not argued. I restored the exact omission in production (submit(facts.affordance, decision, findings)) and the arm went RED: `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ { …(6) }, …(3) ]` / `Number of calls: 1` — called, but with the wrong arguments, which is the blindness this arm exists to remove. Restored from an out-of-tree backup taken and hash-verified BEFORE the edit, never git checkout --, since the file carries this row's uncommitted work: sha256 b5429ee205c792395b946ea6f6344589825311218a874a477c4f3ac28c4110e3 before == after. Mutation was confined to a control-room file for a few seconds; the peer holding full-suite-gate is running the DAEMON suite, which cannot see apps/control-room. Green after restore: 6 passed (6).

implementationPlan.description:
THE LIVE SPEC (DoD 3) — AND READ THIS BEFORE EDITING, BECAUSE THE CLAUSE IS AMBIGUOUS AND ONE READING IS HARMFUL.

preview-approve-live.spec.ts:136-142 is the WALL B arm. It dispatches AS THE OPERATOR with `previewAggregateId(goalId)` and asserts a refusal of PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY. THAT REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND MUST SURVIVE. An aggregate id is still not a receipt id after this fix; the daemon is right and DoD 4 forbids touching it. Read literally, "the WALL B arm asserts Approve COMMITS (not refuses)" would mean making the daemon accept an aggregate id — do not do that, and do not delete the arm to satisfy the sentence.

WHAT THE CLAUSE ACTUALLY WANTS: the spec must now prove the BROWSER'S path commits. The spec already commits for real at :145 with `preview.receiptId`. So keep the aggregate-id case as an explicitly labelled NEGATIVE CONTROL — relabel its comment to say it pins the daemon's refusal of the wrong id, not the browser's behaviour — and make the arm that represents the browser send what the port now sends and COMMIT.

WALL A IS UNCHANGED, and DoD 3 says so: the paired non-operator HUMAN still gets 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION at :132-134. That is the deliberate policy pin from operator ruling comment-18dc557c and is not this row's business.

If after reading the spec you conclude the clause cannot be satisfied without a daemon change, STOP and say so on the row rather than editing the daemon or weakening a control.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 3 satisfied in the sense the step names, and I am flagging the deviation from the clause's literal wording rather than hiding it. DoD 3 reads "the WALL B arm asserts the operator's Approve COMMITS (not refuses)". Taken literally that means making the daemon accept a preview AGGREGATE id where it expects a RECEIPT id. That is a daemon authority change, DoD 4 forbids it, and the refusal is correct: an aggregate id is still not a receipt id after this fix. I did not do it and I did not delete the arm to make the sentence true.

WHAT I DID INSTEAD, which is what step-4 instructs. WALL B keeps its PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY refusal and is relabelled as an explicit NEGATIVE CONTROL pinning the DAEMON's refusal of a wrong id, no longer described as "the aggregate id the browser sends" — after this row the browser does not compose that value at all. The arm at what is now :157, which dispatches preview.receiptId and asserts PREVIEW_DECISION_RECORDED, is relabelled THE BROWSER'S PATH, COMMITTED FOR REAL, because that is now literally the value the Approve button sends: live-needs-you.tsx passes facts.receiptId and preview-port.ts puts it in previewRef verbatim. So the spec does prove the browser's Approve commits.

ONE ASSERTION ADDED, because the negative control could go vacuous: expect(previewAggregateId(goalId)).not.toBe(preview.receiptId). If those two strings ever coincided the wall-B arm would pass while measuring nothing — the same identity-of-fixtures defect that kept this whole row green in preview-port.test.ts.

WALL A UNTOUCHED, deliberately including its comment, which is still true: the paired non-operator HUMAN still gets 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION and the real click still commits nothing. No daemon file touched. Lane execution and its count line are step-5's business.

comments.author: worker-a11dcf70
comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL PASS (step-5). The five questions the step names, in order, answered from the code rather than from intent. One of them changed the code; that change is in this row.

1. "IS THERE ANY OTHER CALLER OF `preview.submit` THAT NOW PASSES THE WRONG ARGUMENT IN THE NEW SECOND POSITION?" There was one, and it is fixed in this row. A positional insertion is the classic silent break, so I grepped every call site rather than trusting the plan's affectedFiles, which named only two files. THREE callers exist: `live-needs-you.tsx:191` (step-3's subject), `preview-port.test.ts` (six sites), and `preview-rejection-invariants.test.tsx:131`, which step-2 did not name. That third one called `submit(FACTS.affordance, "REJECT", [...])` — after the signature change it would have put `"REJECT"` into `receiptId` and the findings array into `decision`, taking the else branch and building a REJECT payload with `previewRef: "REJECT"`. TypeScript would have caught the array-in-decision position, but the arm's own assertion would not have: it asserted a hardcoded `previewRef: "preview:goal-1"`. Fixed to pass `FACTS.receiptId` and to assert that value. `tests/e2e/control-room/lane-preview.ts` matches a `PreviewPort` grep but is a false positive — that is `detectPreviewPort`, a TCP port.

2. "DOES THE REJECT PATH STILL SEND ITS FINDINGS UNCHANGED, AND IS ITS PAYLOAD ARITY STILL EXACTLY WHAT THE DAEMON ADMITS?" Yes to both, and it is pinned in two places rather than one. The `findings.length === 0` guard returning PREVIEW_FINDINGS_REQUIRED at the browser's own layer is untouched, and it still short-circuits before the offer is spent (`expect([built, sent]).toEqual([[], []])`). The REJECT payload is still exactly `{decision, findings, previewRef}` with each finding exactly `{detail, nodeRef}`, asserted by `toEqual` on the whole payload in preview-port.test.ts:79 and again in preview-rejection-invariants.test.tsx by `Object.keys(finding).sort()`. The copy-not-forward behaviour is unchanged and still has its own arm.

3. "CAN `facts.receiptId` EVER BE UNDEFINED AT THE MOMENT THE OPERATOR CLICKS, AND WHAT DOES THE PORT SEND THEN?" It cannot, and the reason is a decoder rather than the type. `PreviewFacts.receiptId` is a non-optional `string`, but a type does not survive a malformed daemon answer, so I traced the runtime path. `projectionOf` (live-preview.ts:138) requires `text(record["receiptId"])`, and `text` demands `typeof === "string" && length > 0 && length <= 4096` with no NUL. A receipt whose `receiptId` is missing, empty or non-string makes the whole projection null, `mapPreviewAnswer` answers `invalidResponse()` (status ERROR), and `previewOfferFor` returns null on `preview.status !== "PREVIEW"` — so NO CARD RENDERS. There is no Approve button to click. The empty-string case is the interesting one and it is closed by `length > 0` specifically, not by the type.

4. "DOES ANY OTHER PORT IN THIS DIRECTORY READ AN ID OFF THE AFFORDANCE THE SAME WAY `previewRefOf` DID?" One does, and per the step this is a comment on this row rather than a new one. `escalation-port.ts:35` reads `affordance["targetAggregateId"]` into `subjectRef` and synthesises `escalationRef` from it. That is NOT the same defect: `escalation.decide`'s payload keys are `["decision", "escalationRef", "subjectRef"]` (daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:133) and the daemon's escalation offer targets the NODE, so the offer's target IS the subject the payload wants. The preview case was a mismatch because the offer targets the preview AGGREGATE while the payload wants the RECEIPT — two different identifiers for the same subject. The other `targetAggregateId` reads in this directory (needs-you-deploy, needs-you-escalation, needs-you-model, needs-you-preview, needs-you-release) only MATCH an offer by target, which is correct use.

5. "AFTER THIS CHANGE, DOES THE OPERATOR'S APPROVE BUTTON ACTUALLY COMMIT A PREVIEW DECISION, AND WHICH ARM PROVES IT END TO END RATHER THAN AT THE PORT BOUNDARY?" Yes, and I want to be precise about what is proven by ONE arm versus by TWO joined arms, because the honest answer is the second.

The browser lane's committed arm dispatches `preview.receiptId` and the daemon records `disposition: "COMMITTED"` in `/activity/read` — that is a real end-to-end commit against a real running preview, printed as `LIVE_DRIVE_DECISION`. But it dispatches over `decideLanePreview`, an HTTP helper, NOT by clicking the button. The DoD 2 unit arm proves the button sends exactly `facts.receiptId`. The chain "button → receipt id → COMMITTED" is therefore joined at the value, not observed in a single arm.

THAT GAP IS NOT CLOSEABLE BY THIS ROW, and the reason is deliberate policy rather than an oversight. The spec's real click is made by the paired browser HUMAN, which WALL A refuses with 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION — the operator-principal fence from ruling comment-18dc557c, which this row's description explicitly excludes and DoD 4 forbids touching. So a single arm that clicks the real button and observes a COMMITTED verdict cannot exist while that fence stands, and manufacturing one would mean widening the fence. I am stating the limit rather than claiming the stronger result.
